# Product name

One sentence explaining who the product helps, what it does, and the primary outcome.

One short paragraph explaining the product model or defining boundary.

[Product page](https://example.com) · [Report an issue](https://example.com/issues)

## Status

State the current version, release channel, installation availability, and any material distribution gap.

## Highlights

- Describe a concrete capability.
- Describe a second concrete capability.
- Name an important safety, privacy, or control boundary.

## Quick start

### Install

List prerequisites and the shortest safe installation path.

```sh
npm ci
```

### First workflow

1. Complete the first meaningful action.
2. Confirm the visible result.
3. Link deeper guidance when needed.

## How it works

Explain product-specific concepts and decision rules only when the quick start is not enough.

## Privacy and permissions

Explain local and hosted data handling, network behavior, and required or optional permissions. Link the complete policy when one exists.

## Known limitations

- Name a meaningful unsupported surface or environmental constraint.
- Describe a failure boundary that users should understand before relying on the product.

## Development

List the authoritative verification and packaging commands.

```sh
npm test
npm run build
```

State where generated artifacts go and whether the command publishes anything.

## App Stylr

This product follows [App Stylr v1.2.0](https://github.com/kylbutlr/app-stylr/tree/v1.2.0). Use the [Visual Reference](https://kylbutlr.com/app-stylr) to understand shared tokens and states, then document only semantic compatibility differences in `docs/app-stylr-exceptions.md`.

## Support

Link the public support destination and explain what safe diagnostic information to include. Never request credentials, private URLs, or confidential captures.

## License

State the actual license and link the repository's license file before publishing.
